name: AIB Data Centers Inc.

profile.description: AIB Data Centers (renamed from BlockchAIn Digital Infrastructure on June 25, 2026) develops data-center capacity for AI and high-performance computing, operating through its subsidiary One Blockchain LLC at a facility in Spartanburg County, South Carolina. On September 30, 2026 it signed a binding 12-year agreement with AI cloud company Nebius for 50 MW of critical IT capacity, supported by a 15-year, 65 MW electric service agreement. In September it also acquired two Texas sites with 55 MW of energized or contracted power. The company de-energized its legacy Bitcoin hosting in June 2026, so Q2 2026 revenue fell 39% to $2.9M. CEO Jerry Tang leads the pivot. Market cap is about $65M.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): the company has pivoted from Bitcoin-mining hosting to AI/HPC colocation, de-energizing substantially all Bitcoin operations on June 5, 2026 and signing a binding 12-year, 50 MW agreement with Nebius on September 30, 2026. That opens a new revenue stream, although it does not yet produce revenue [2][3]. AI Deployment (1/2): AIB is building infrastructure for AI customers, but no AI capacity is operating or generating revenue yet [2]. Market Share (0/2): it is a sub-scale entrant with $17.1M of trailing revenue in a market led by far larger hyperscale and neocloud developers [6]. Product Pipeline (1/2): there are 570 MW of identified capacity potential and the Texas sites, but about 505 MW across five sites has no definitive agreements and the Nebius service date is undisclosed [2][3]. R&D Intensity (0/1): no R&D spending is reported [5].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): CEO Jerry Tang describes the strategy as 'secure power in attractive markets and convert that power into long-term contracted revenue with leading AI' customers [2]. That is a business plan rather than a purpose. Community Impact (0/2): no community or charitable programs were found. Employee Retention (0/2): the company has 3 full-time employees and was still searching for a Chief Operating Officer with large-scale data-center experience, so there is no retention evidence [2][6]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP returned no insider transaction data for AIB [5].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically using growth-sleeve weights (5-year revenue CAGR and Forward PEG unavailable and excluded; weighted sum 1.00 of 6 = 1.7, rounded to 2). The only positive is an essentially debt-free balance sheet: D/E of 0.03% scores 1.00, with $52.8M of cash and $82.7M of equity after a $63.3M raise [1][6]. Every other metric scores 0.00: ROE of -9.8% (2x weight), revenue growth of -38.6% YoY, profit margin of -26.5%, and a negative forward P/E of -1.60 [6]. Liquidity is about $1.5M per day (1.77M shares x $0.85), only just above the $1M floor [6].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): AIB is building AI infrastructure. Power, land and cooled data-center capacity are physical inputs that AI demand increases rather than displaces, as shown by Nebius taking 50 MW under a 12-year term [2][3]. Its risks are execution, financing and customer concentration, not AI substitution [3]. AI Opportunity (0/1): no AI-hosting revenue has been recognized yet; Q2 2026 revenue of $2.9M came from the legacy hosting business during the transition, so the tiebreaker point is withheld until Nebius revenue begins [1].

infinite_game.summary: AIB is an opportunistic power-and-real-estate play that has rebranded from Bitcoin mining to AI hosting as the economics shifted. Through Sinek's lens, the pivot was driven by power costs exceeding Bitcoin hosting prices, not by a lasting cause. The organization is too young and too small (3 employees, a COO still being recruited, a minority-independent board) to show trusting teams or long-term identity. The Nebius contract is a real milestone, but this is a company playing to survive the next financing round, not to keep playing for decades.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): management's stated aim is to turn secured power into long-term contracted revenue with AI customers, a purely commercial objective with no vision of a better future state [2]. The name change from BlockchAIn to AIB Data Centers follows market demand rather than an enduring purpose [4].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): with 3 full-time employees, an open search for a Chief Operating Officer and a board where fewer than half of directors are independent, there is no basis for a high-trust organization yet [2][4][6].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): no management commentary was found that references learning from competing AI data-center developers [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): AIB abandoned its core Bitcoin hosting business in June 2026, accepting a 39% revenue decline, to reposition as an AI/HPC colocation provider [1][2]. The move was decisive, but it was triggered by power costs exceeding what Bitcoin customers would pay rather than by a just cause, so it falls short of Sinek's transformative standard.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): leadership gave up near-term hosting revenue to pursue long-dated AI leases, and structured the Nebius build with customer prepayments, project debt and preferred equity to limit common-equity dilution [1][3]. These are costly near-term choices for long-term capability, though early-stage and unproven.

investment_thesis: AIB has converted a power position into a contracted AI customer. The binding 12-year agreement with Nebius for 50 MW of critical IT capacity, with two five-year renewal options, sits on a site backed by a 15-year, 65 MW electric service agreement that needs no significant additional grid upgrades [2][3]. Financing is planned through customer prepayments, project-level debt and preferred equity to limit common dilution, and the company starts with $52.8M of cash and essentially no debt [1][3]. September's acquisition of two Texas sites with 55 MW of energized or contracted power and a 570 MW identified pipeline offer further options at a roughly $65M market cap [2][3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is execution and financing at micro-cap scale. Revenue fell 39% YoY to $2.9M in Q2 2026 after Bitcoin hosting was shut down, the company posted a $0.07 loss per share versus a $0.01 consensus loss, and Q1 gross margin had already compressed to 12% from 27% on energy costs [1]. Building 50 MW for Nebius will take substantial capital whose amount and timing are undisclosed, and the contract value and service-start date are also undisclosed [3]. About 505 MW of the pipeline has no definitive agreements [2]. The share price of about $0.85 is down sharply from its 50-day average of $1.29 even after the Nebius announcement, and liquidity of about $1.5M per day sits barely above IOWN's floor [6]. Fewer than half of directors are independent [4].
key_catalysts: Closing of project-level debt and preferred-equity financing for the 50 MW Nebius build, which would de-risk delivery and limit common dilution [3]
Disclosure of the Nebius contract value and service-start date, and initial recognition of AI-hosting revenue to replace the shut-down Bitcoin business [1][3]
Conversion of the 570 MW identified pipeline, including the 55 MW across two Texas sites, into additional binding leases [2][3]
key_risks: Financing risk: the multi-hundred-million-dollar scale of a 50 MW AI build far exceeds the $52.8M cash balance, and failing to secure project debt or preferred equity could force heavy dilution [1][3]
Customer concentration: future revenue would depend almost entirely on Nebius, a single neocloud tenant, over a 12-year term [3]
Execution and governance risk: 3 employees, no COO in place yet, and a minority-independent board must deliver a complex data-center build on schedule [2][4]
